chalisa.do1: Narmadā is a worshipped goddess; her glory is great and boundless.
Poets and noble devotees describe it in a chālīsā.
chalisa.do2: By service to her, great sins are always wiped away;
doing japa and giving gifts on her banks, people ever gain knowledge.
chalisa.cau1: Victory, victory, victory to Narmadā Bhavānī. The whole world knows your glory.
chalisa.cau2: The Mother came forth from Amarakaṇṭaka; she is the giver of every siddhi and the nine treasures.
chalisa.cau3: When Narmadā Bhavānī appeared, it was in the form of a maiden, a mine of every virtue.
chalisa.cau4: On a saptamī, with the sun in Makara, on a Sunday, in the Aśvinī nakṣatra, in the month of Māgha, you descended to earth.
chalisa.cau5: A crocodile, your mount, adorns you; you are seated on a lotus flower.
chalisa.cau6: Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva meditate on you; only then do they gain the fruit their hearts desire.
chalisa.cau7: At the sight of you sins are cut away; millions of devotees bathe in you every day.
chalisa.cau8: Whoever meditates on you every day goes to the world of Rudra.
chalisa.cau9: Crocodiles find happiness in you, and at their last hour they attain the supreme state.
chalisa.cau10: A crown always adorns your head, and anklets ever shine on your feet.
chalisa.cau11: You flow with a murmuring sound, Mother; you take away sin and suffering, Mother.
chalisa.cau12: The Mother flows from east to west, and peacocks dance.
chalisa.cau13: The sage Śaunaka sings your virtues; Sūta and others sing your fame.
chalisa.cau14: Śiva and Gaṇeśa too sing your virtues; all the hosts of gods meditate on you.
chalisa.cau15: Millions of holy places lie on the banks of the Narmadā; all of them are called removers of sorrow.
chalisa.cau16: The Mother fulfils the heart's desires and ever takes away all sorrow.
chalisa.cau17: At Kanakhala is the glory of the Gaṅgā; at Kurukṣetra the glory of the Sarasvatī;
chalisa.cau18: but the Narmadā's glory is found in village and forest; the Mother ever dwells in blessing.
chalisa.cau19: By bathing in you just once, the many generations of a person are carried across.
chalisa.cau20: You are the daughter of Mekala, you are Revā; the gods worship you every day.
chalisa.cau21: Jaṭāśaṅkarī is your name; you have carried millions of people across.
chalisa.cau22: You are Narmadā, Somodbhavā, born of the moon; you are Revā, who frees from sin.
chalisa.cau23: Your glory cannot be told; Mother, your greatness is beyond praising.
chalisa.cau24: The power of the water in you is very great, Mother; it is lovely and gives happiness.
chalisa.cau25: Your course is like a serpent's; your glory is utterly boundless.
chalisa.cau26: Even a heavy bone that falls into you turns to stone at the touch of your excellent water.
chalisa.cau27: Whoever bathes in the Yamunā gains the fruit in seven days.
chalisa.cau28: The Sarasvatī gives it in three days, and the Gaṅgā at once, right after bathing;
chalisa.cau29: but by the mere sight of Revā a person gains the fruit to his heart's content.
chalisa.cau30: Your glory is very great, and men and women sing it.
chalisa.cau31: Whoever bathes in you every day is honoured in the world of Rudra.
chalisa.cau32: Herbs shine in splendour on the banks, and charming sights always adorn them.
chalisa.cau33: A fragrant breeze blows along the banks, and it takes away the pain of the human body.
chalisa.cau34: The glory of every ghāṭ is great; not even poets can sing it all.
chalisa.cau35: I do not know how to worship you; I have no other support.
chalisa.cau36: Be pleased with me, my Mother; you alone, Mother, are the giver of liberation.
chalisa.cau37: The honour of whoever reads this every day ever grows.
chalisa.cau38: Whoever sings it a hundred times gains learning, wealth and riches.
chalisa.cau39: Whoever reads it countless times has his heart's desire fulfilled.
chalisa.cau40: Narmadā dwells in every heart; here, there and everywhere is Narmadā.
chalisa.do3: Whoever brings devotion into his heart and does japa,
by the Mother's grace his anguish is taken away.
